newsitem.title: USA: Jury returns 3 verdicts against Honeywell.
newsitem.headline: Jury returns 3 verdicts against Honeywell.

text.p: In litigation between Honeywell Inc's satellite systems operation and American Flywheel Systems Inc, a Phoenix jury returned three verdicts against Honeywell for $38 million dollars and one verdict in favor of it for relief that will be determined by the court, Honeywell said.
The case stemmed from the development contract signed in 1993 for an electromechanical flywheel battery, Honeywell said.

Honeywell said it originally filed suit in September 1994 because of American Flywheel's failure to pay for work performed and because the parties were unable to agree on their respective rights and obligations under the contract.
AFS countersued, alleging breach of the development agreement.

"We will bring motions to contest these verdicts and resolve the remaining issues. We expect these motions will be heard by the court over the next several months and resolved sometime in 1997," John Leshinski, counsel for Honeywell said.
Honeywell makes control systems for home, industrial and aerospace markets.
